statement: A service/provider dispatch layer that already distinguishes 'delivered' from 'did not complete' MUST further distinguish, within 'did not complete', an INFRASTRUCTURE-level failure (every routed/fallback inference provider unreachable) from a CONTENT/GOVERNANCE-level failure (grounding failure, empty response, a real refusal) — using the one exact, narrow signal the underlying sovereign-inference layer already emits for the infrastructure case, never a broad heuristic guess. The distinction must be carried as a structured, machine-checkable field (an error code), not only as prose in a message string, all the way to the operator-facing surface and to the HTTP status code of any route that exposes it (infrastructure -> 5xx, content/governance -> 4xx). Conflating the two lets a transient provider outage misrepresent itself as a regression in the service/agent that merely depends on inference — costing operator trust and mis-directed debugging effort.
classification: A layering gap: the dispatch layer's own success/failure taxonomy (DELIVERED vs UNRESOLVED, established by Repair D) was correct as far as it went, but treated every 'did not complete' failure as one undifferentiated case — losing the one signal (the sovereign-inference layer's single distinguishable 'all providers failed' throw) that would have let it tell an infrastructure outage apart from a genuine content/governance failure.

canaries.assertion: isProviderUnavailableError() matches ONLY the exact callStage() 'all providers failed' throw shape, never a single-provider failure or an unrelated error; describeProviderLadderAvailability() never returns a credential value; the Architect route maps the classified failure to HTTP 503, and every other failure to HTTP 400.

An INFERENCE_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE Architect/Advisor dispatch failure resolves the outcome status UNRESOLVED with errorCode set, never REFUSED and never a silent DELIVERED; a non-infrastructure failure resolves UNRESOLVED without the errorCode.

occurrences.defect: Every technical provider-dispatch failure (infrastructure outage or genuine content/grounding failure) produced the same generic 'gate allowed but provider invocation did not complete' reason, with no structured way for a caller to tell them apart; the Architect route additionally mapped every such failure to HTTP 400, misrepresenting an infrastructure condition as a client error.

notes: Companion concern, same resolution, not itself promoted to a separate candidate here: a dispatch layer's 'immutable evidence reference' (a hash/commitment/artifact id) and 'operator-visible display output' (the real prose/proposal) are two distinct obligations that must both be satisfied on a successful dispatch — satisfying one must never come at the cost of the other. Watch for this shape recurring in any future provider-dispatch layer that computes a receipt-safe reference from a real result.

Generic shape to watch for elsewhere: any layer built on top of `services/constitutional/modelRouter.ts::callSovereign`/`callStage` that catches its own errors — the SAME `isProviderUnavailableError` classifier applies verbatim; a caller must never re-derive its own heuristic for 'is this a provider outage'.
